Learned counsel for the petitioner would further submit that pursuant to the order passed by this Court on 10.11.2023 the Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:5449 petitioner and the victim have appeared before this Court and recorded their statements wherein the victim has stated that she is living with the petitioner peacefully as wife in her matrimonial house and she has no objection if the criminal proceedings are quashed.
He would further submit that the case has now been fixed for recording of the statement of the accused in the criminal trial before the trial Court.
6. The victim has also entered appearance through counsel who pleads no objection if the criminal proceeding initiated against the petitioner is quashed.
7. On the other hand, learned State counsel would oppose the submission and submit that since the offence has been committed against the society it cannot be quashed.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
9. A bare perusal of the record would show that victim has solemnized marriage with the petitioner for the first time on 03.02.2022.

After she has attained majority, she again solemnized marriage with the petitioner on 03.02.2023 which has also been registered on 17.02.2023 before the Registrar (Marriage) and from their wedlock a baby was also born in January, 2024, in her cross-examination before the trial Court she has stated contrary to the case of the prosecution, has also stated that she has love affair with the petitioner, she has voluntarily gone with the petitioner and he has not committed any sexual assault on her on the date of incident.

10. Considering the entire factual matrix of the case it is quite vivid that the victim was in love affair with the petitioner and now they have already solemnized marriage and a baby child was also born from their wedlock and in the evidence the victim has also deposed against the prosecution.

As such,
it is directed that the learned trial Court should frame question on this aspect of the matter also while framing questions as provided under Section 313 Cr.P.C. as now the case is fixed for recording of statement of the accused under Section 313 of the Cr.P.C. on 21.02.2024 and Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:5449 if the accused intends to examine the defence witness after completion of prosecution witness, he may be allowed to examine witnesses including the victim who is now wife of the accused as defence witness.

11. It is well settled position of law that the statement recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. is the vital defence of the accused which cannot be ignored by the trial Court as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Jai Prakash Tiwari vs. State of Madhya Pradesh 1 wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court has highlighted the aims and objects of Section 313 Cr.P.C.

This Court in the case of Satbir Singh v. State of Haryana, (2021) 6 SCC 1, while emphasising upon the significance of Section 313 CrPC, has delineated the duty of the trial Court and held thus:
"22.

entities.text: Satbir Singh v. State of Haryana, (2021) 6 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a matter of grave concern that, often, trial courts record the statement of an accused under Section 313 CrPC in a very casual and cursory manner, without specifically questioning the accused as to his defence.
It ought to be noted that the examination of an accused under Section 313 CrPC cannot be treated as a mere procedural formality, as it is based on the fundamental principle of fairness.
This provision incorporates the valuable principle of natural justice -- "audi alteram partem", as it enables the accused to offer an explanation for the incriminatory material appearing against him.
Therefore, it imposes an obligation on the part of the court to question the accused fairly, with care and caution.
The court must put incriminating circumstances before the accused and seek his response.

A duty is also cast on the counsel of the accused to prepare his defence, since the inception of the trial, with due caution..."
30.
Moreover, it is the solemn duty of the courts below to consider the defence of the accused.
The same must be considered with caution and must be scrutinised by application of mind by the judge.
The Court may accept or reject the same, however it cannot be done cursorily.
The reasoning and the application of mind must be reflected in writing.
However, from the observations extracted above, it is clear that the courts below have failed to undertake this solemn duty.
Rather, the evidence of the accused has been dealt by the Court in a casual manner."
1 AIR 2022 SC3601 Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:5449 12.

It is also directed that the learned trial Court while deciding the criminal trial will consider the subsequent events, particularly the marriage of the petitioner with the victim, birth of child from their wedlock, fact that victim is residing in the matrimonial house peacefully and also the evidence of the victim wherein she has denied commission of offence and also the statement recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. as well as the statement of defence witnesses, if any recorded.
13. With the aforesaid observation and direction, the Cr.M.P. is disposed off.
